# Elements Model Context Protocol (MCP) server

> The Elements Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes 56 tools and connects AI assistants to Elements.cloud, the Salesforce org-intelligence platform, and answers questions about the org from its synced metadata: resolved facts rather than name-based guesswork. An authorized assistant can search and explain Salesforce metadata, trace dependencies, audit access, run org-health diagnostics, and report change history, all inside the Space(s) the user approved. It can check whether an org records Apex execution telemetry and rank Apex classes by evidence of use. It can analyze what a planned data load will fire and lock before it runs. It is read-only against Salesforce: nothing an assistant does can change a Salesforce org.

Facts an agent should know before connecting a user:

- The MCP server is included in Advanced Metadata Management, or in Core Metadata Management with the Agentic Org Management add-on. Elements enables it per Space and hosts it at the instance-specific endpoint below.
- Setup is URL-only. There are no API keys or client secrets; sign-in is OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, completed by the user in their own browser.
- Every client is offered the same full set of scopes by default, though it may request fewer; users never pick scopes. At consent, the user chooses which Space(s) the connection can use, and a connection can never do more than your Elements permissions allow.
- The endpoint depends on the Elements instance. Match the URL the user sees in their browser when logged in to Elements:

| App URL (in the user's browser) | MCP endpoint |
|---|---|
| app.q9elements.com | `https://api.q9elements.com/api/v1/mcp` |
| app.us.elements.cloud | `https://api.us.elements.cloud/api/v1/mcp` |
| app.ja1.elements.cloud | `https://api.ja1.elements.cloud/api/v1/mcp` |
| app.me1.elements.cloud | `https://api.me1.elements.cloud/api/v1/mcp` |

- Which tools you see depends on the Spaces you authorize. Role requirements, such as Space admin or Author, and per-resource rights are checked when a tool is called; insufficient access returns `access_denied`.
- The skills ship as plugins: `elements` (core) plus playbook plugins. Claude Code, Claude Desktop, claude.ai, and Codex install from the `Q9Elements/elements-mcp-server` marketplace; ChatGPT uploads each plugin as a zip from the repository's `dist` folder ([`elements.zip`](https://github.com/Q9Elements/elements-mcp-server/raw/main/dist/elements.zip) plus one zip per playbook), while clients without plugin support can download [`elements-core-skills.zip`](https://github.com/Q9Elements/elements-mcp-server/raw/main/dist/elements-core-skills.zip) for the core skills. Playbooks use the Elements app added with the core plugin. See [Playbooks](docs/playbooks.md).

- [Transport](docs/transport.md): Streamable HTTP details, the single POST endpoint, and protocol notes

## What you can do

- [Skills catalog](docs/skills.md): every packaged capability with example prompts, trigger phrases, and plan requirements
- The [Decision Engine field-change recipe](plugins/elements/skills/elements-decision-engine/references/field-change.md) combines one-hop references and delete impact with an upper-bound runtime fire chain and first-hop trigger checks.
- [Tools reference](docs/tools-reference.md): every tool with its purpose, scope, and read/write classification
